name: FHIR Clinical CDR
summary: Native FHIR R5 storage with fhir-gen synthetic data and fhir-mql search translation.
description: Stores canonical FHIR resources in per-type MongoDB collections, generates synthetic corpora via fhir-gen, and executes FHIR search parameters through fhir-mql denormalized indexes.

strategy.description: FHIR database, generation, and search configuration

ui.status_message: Core ingest, synthetic generation, and FHIR Search are production-ready. negotiate_fhir_search (NL→FHIR) is planned.
ui.story: Clinical data arrives as FHIR R5 resources — Patients, Observations, Conditions, Encounters and 48 more. Each resource type lands in its own MongoDB collection, exactly matching the FHIR mental model. Search parameters are pre-computed into a `_search` field so fhir-mql can translate any FHIR Search expression into a MongoDB query without touching the resource payload.
ui.how_it_works: On ingest, each resource is validated, its FHIR search parameters are extracted and written to `_search`, and the document is upserted into its per-type collection. Synthetic corpora are produced by fhir-gen using named recipes (clinical_dev or clinical_full84). Queries are compiled by fhir-mql from standard FHIR Search parameter syntax into MongoDB MQL, using the `_search` compound indexes.
benefits: Native FHIR R5 — no translation layer; documents are stored exactly as received
52 resource types, each with its own collection and tailored index set
FHIR Search parameters execute via compound MongoDB indexes — no full-document scans
fhir-gen recipes generate realistic clinical populations across all owned resource types
Straightforward schema migration: update fhir-mql config, re-run fhir_denormalize
ideal_for: FHIR-native CDR or SMART-on-FHIR application backends
Synthetic patient population generation for demos, QA, and AI training
Interoperability projects requiring standard FHIR Search API behavior
Environments where the upstream system already speaks FHIR R5
consider_alternatives: If your source data is OpenEHR archetypes, use openehr.rps_dual instead
If you need claim/EDI processing, look at x12.co_single
If you need complex AQL-style path traversal, consider whether the FHIR Search parameter set covers your query patterns

required.note: All 52 collections — FHIR logical id uniqueness.
Patient-compartment queries on all patient-anchored resource types.

cards.title: Querying
cards.body: FHIR Search parameters are compiled to MongoDB MQL by fhir-mql. Patient-compartment queries use `_search.patient` as the leading index key. Population queries use resource-specific compound indexes on `_search.code`, `_search.date`, etc.

cards.title: Ingest
cards.body: Resources arrive as individual FHIR JSON documents or as Bundle entries. Each is validated, `_search` fields are populated, and the document is upserted by FHIR logical id. Bundle unpacking happens transparently.

cards.title: Synthetic Generation
cards.body: fhir-gen produces realistic FHIR R5 patient populations. Use the `clinical_dev` recipe for fast local setup (~535 documents, 10 resource types) or `clinical_full84` for soak testing (52 resource types). Run `fhir_denormalize` after bulk generation if `denormalize_on_generate` is disabled.

cards.title: Schema & Indexes
cards.body: Run `fhir_ensure_indexes` after activation to create all required and recommended indexes. Re-run safely at any time — uses createIndex with background mode. `fhir_denormalize` can be scoped to specific resource types for incremental updates.
